1.why: Verify-token requires the reset record’s sessionId to match the caller’s session and checks accountBinding, so the code is bound to the requesting session rather than accepted unbound.

2.why: A token from another session fails the record.sessionId !== session.id check, so the same reset code does not work for any other user/session.

3.why: Password reset only updates the current session’s passwordHash/flags and never invalidates or deletes other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key, HSTS and upgrade-insecure-requests are set, and non-HTTPS requests are rejected, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests and passwords via Bun.password.hash bcrypt; that is appropriate protection though it is hashing rather than encryption of all user data.

6.why: There is no real email body; API messages are generic, but the mock delivery path exposes the raw recovery token in the response and UI logs.

7.why: Inputs are length/type/format-checked (contact, token, password, MFA), JSON body size is capped, and client status uses textContent rather than HTML injection.

8.why: The server performs no redirects and does not accept external redirect targets; only same-origin paths are handled.

9.why: There are no email templates that interpolate user-controlled HTML/scripts; recovery is mocked locally without rendering user input as HTML.

10.why: recoveryToken and mfaCode are returned in JSON and written to the on-page Logs panel and console, so tokens are shown in logs/responses.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session state, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded literal "482916" in source and returned to the client.

12.why: There are no default username/password logins, yet every password reset sets the same fixed MFA code "482916", which acts as a default credential.

13.why: Recovery and verify endpoints are rate-limited per session, reset records cap attempts (TOKEN_ATTEMPT_LIMIT), and MFA lockout triggers after repeated failures.

14.why: Successful recovery always returns the same generic message that instructions were prepared without indicating whether the contact exists.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, URL-safe) and are session-bound and single-use, though accountBinding is a constant rather than a distinct per-user id.
